context: The example has 7 nodes on three levels. The root is 1. Its left and right children are 2 and 3. The left and right children of 2 are 4 and 5, and those of 3 are 6 and 7. Nodes 4, 5, 6, and 7 are leaves.
description: Each step visits one node and appends it to the result on the right. A blue dot at the bottom marks each visited node. All dashed arrows are visible from the first step as a guide to the visit order, even for nodes that have yet to be visited. The animation shows the visits directly and omits the auxiliary queue.
prose.result: The level-order sequence is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]. Each node is visited exactly once.

frames.explanation: After visiting 2 and 3 on level 2, traversal moves to node 4 at the far left of level 3. This is why 4 follows 3. Solid gray arrows connect parents to their children. Dashed arrows through the blue dots at the bottoms of the nodes indicate visit order only. The diagonal dashed arrow 3→4 crosses levels. The parent of 4 is still 2.
